title: This Scorpion Drops Its Tail to Escape. It Can Never Poop Again

scenes.text: This scorpion can snap off its own tail. The price is horrifying.
Grab one of these small South American scorpions by the tail and it wriggles for a few seconds, then breaks free. The tail keeps thrashing, as if it's still trying to sting.
The predator gets a decoy. But a scorpion's anus isn't on its body. It's near the tip of the tail.
The tail never grows back. So the scorpion can never poop again. Scientists watched their bodies slowly swell.
It still lives about eight months, catching small prey with its claws.
It's mostly adult males that do it. Eight months is long enough to find a mate. For them, that's worth the tail.

description:
Some scorpions escape predators by breaking off their own tail, and with it their anus.
Scorpions of the South American genus Ananteris can sever the tail at one of several weak points when grabbed; the detached tail keeps moving as a decoy. Because a scorpion's digestive tract ends near the tip of the tail and the tail never regrows, the animal can no longer defecate, yet it survives for around eight months, long enough to mate. The behaviour, seen in 14 species and mostly in adult males, was described in PLOS ONE in 2015 by Camilo Mattoni and colleagues, including Lorenzo Prendini of the American Museum of Natural History.
Would you take that deal to escape?
subject: scorpion
first_comment: Researchers estimate 5 to 8 percent of these scorpions in the wild are walking around with a stump. Worth it to escape, or not?
